To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of a resistively terminated ladder is possible with a cascade of gyrator-capacitors, with all gyrator grounded, using a minimal number of capacitors all of which are equal.

a capacitor cascade synthesis for real filters is possible with a minimum number of capacitors, all of which can have a value equal to one-half of the terminating resistance, and that this synthesis can be performed in a manner which is both systematic and simple.
the following are true: (1) A new class of all-capacitor ladder networks is introduced that are derived from the conventional ladder networks by the use of gyrators.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a synthesis method for integrated circuits which is based upon the use of non-reciprocity in the design process.
the synthesis of nonreciprocal filters, and in particular with the design of integrated filters using a minimum number and a minimum number of different capacitor values.
the synthesis of passive, resistively terminated, lossless networks with a prescribed frequency characteristic, using a minimum number or a prescribed number of elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesis presented here is the most general synthesis for the design of integrated filters.
the capacitor cascade synthesis is a very attractive alternative to the ladder and image parameter synthesis for integrated realizations of low-pass filters.
the capacitor-gyrator structure is a very attractive realization of the ladder filter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a minimal synthesis of a resistively terminated ladder filter can be achieved using a cascade of capacitor sections, with all sections having the same capacitor value and the number of capacitor sections being equal to the number of transmission zeros of the even part of the admittance of the ladder.
the theory of non-reciprocals is applicable to the design of filters for integrated circuits.
the gyrator is the only active element necessary for the realization of a lossless ladder filter, with all gyrator terminals grounded and with all capacitors equal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of a filter is reduced to a set of simple algebraic equations.
the gyrator can be used to realize a capacitor cascade synthesis of a filter with the gyrator being grounded.
this synthesis is a very efficient method to realize filters with a large number of elements, as it uses only a few capacitors, all of which are identical and grounded.
